commands.author: yetval

target.title: auto-reply: /export-session lets allowed non-owners write outside the workspace
target.body:
## Summary
`/export-session` accepts an output path from an authorized chat sender and writes it verbatim after `path.resolve`. An allowed non-owner sender can use an absolute path or traversal path to create or clobber any file writable by the OpenClaw process, outside the workspace export area.

## Environment
- Commit: e90bf318292759ff53a6bb35e3fee75242df1236 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: auto-reply text command `/export-session`

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a session store entry and transcript for an active session.
2. Invoke the real `/export-session` command handler with `isAuthorizedSender: true`, `senderIsOwner: false`, and an absolute output path outside the workspace.
3. Check whether the requested outside path was created.

## Expected
Sensitive session export writes should be owner-only, and a supplied output path should be confined to the workspace export directory in the same spirit as `/export-trajectory`.

## Actual
The command accepts the non-owner authorized sender and writes the HTML export to the absolute path outside the workspace.

## Root cause (if known)
`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-info.ts` gates `/export-session` only on `isAuthorizedSender` before calling the exporter:

```ts
if (!params.command.isAuthorizedSender) {
  logVerbose(
    `Ignoring /export-session from unauthorized sender: ${params.command.senderId || "<unknown>"}`,
  );
  return { shouldContinue: false };
}
return { shouldContinue: false, reply: await buildExportSessionReply(params) };
```

`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-export-session.ts` then resolves and writes the sender path directly:

```ts
let outputPath = args.outputPath
  ? path.resolve(
      args.outputPath.startsWith("~")
        ? args.outputPath.replace("~", process.env.HOME ?? "")
        : args.outputPath,
    )
  : path.join(params.workspaceDir, defaultFileName);

const outputDir = path.dirname(outputPath);
await fsp.mkdir(outputDir, { recursive: true });

if (args.outputPath) {
  await fsp.writeFile(outputPath, html, "utf-8");
}
```

## Sibling surfaces
`/export-trajectory` is more constrained in the router: it calls both `rejectUnauthorizedCommand(params, "/export-trajectory")` and `rejectNonOwnerCommand(params, "/export-trajectory")` before building the export request. I did not see the equivalent owner gate on `/export-session`.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: Authorized non-owner `/export-session` can write an absolute path outside the workspace.
Real environment tested: OpenClaw source runtime at e90bf318292759ff53a6bb35e3fee75242df1236
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/f3/export-session-path-write.ts`
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (buggy, origin/main e90bf318292759ff53a6bb35e3fee75242df1236)
senderIsOwner=false
isAuthorizedSender=true
reply="Session exported | File: /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/f3/outside-workspace/non-owner-export.html | Entries: 1"
outsideWorkspace=true
outsideFileWritten=true
outsideFile=/tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/f3/outside-workspace/non-owner-export.html

# EXPECTED (correct behavior on identical inputs)
senderIsOwner=false
isAuthorizedSender=true
outsideWorkspace=false
outsideFileWritten=false
reply="You are not authorized to use this command."
```
Observed result after fix: The live command path accepted an authorized non-owner sender and created the requested file outside the workspace.
What was not tested: I did not verify every chat transport; this drove the shared auto-reply command handler and exporter directly.
